experiments.scope: The exact blake3-r3-prefix-v1 target. The program regenerates the bit-sliced straight line of proof.md Section 3 and runs, per trial, one attempt of the search of proof.md Section 5 at width 22: 256 trails per batch, points are 22-bit values whose message is 0^32 || LE32(x), planes 22..255 reset to 0 after each step, distinguished when physical planes 0 and 1 are zero, cap 36, 14 batches, starts R + i from one random word (SHAKE-256 of the trial seed, a reproducible stand-in for the attack's random word), a dictionary table and the recovery of Section 5.6 with the plain three-round compression. It returns the pair found by the recovery or two nulls.
experiments.hypothesis: If the 22-bit chain behaves as a random function (premise H_rand at reduced width), a trial succeeds with probability about 0.535 (ideal-function control of the same search, 2,139 of 4,000 attempts, 95 percent interval 0.519 to 0.550): about 136.9 of 256 organizer-recomputed successes, standard deviation 8.0. A success is a 22-bit partial match, not a collision. Observations (untrusted): batches, distinguished points, cut trails, merges, Robin Hood merges. Nothing about cost is inferred from the run.

experiments.scope: The exact blake3-r3-prefix-v1 target. Per trial 256 random planes (SHAKE-256 of the trial seed) are the starting points of 256 trails, the regenerated straight line of proof.md Section 3 runs eight chained full-width steps of g, and the first pair (step-major order) of distinct evaluated inputs whose images agree on the 22 low bits is returned; the two inputs are recomputed from the seed with the plain three-round compression.
experiments.hypothesis: If the images of the 2,048 evaluated inputs of a trial are uniform on 22 bits, a trial succeeds with probability 1 - prod_{i<2048}(1 - i/2^22) = 0.39337: about 100.7 of 256 organizer-recomputed successes, standard deviation 7.8. A success is a 22-bit partial match, not a collision; it also checks the full-width straight line through the organizer's digest. Observation (untrusted): the number of steps run.
